title: fix(plugin-list,plugin-calendar): a list's calendar view fetches the days it shows, walked in fetch batches (objectui#12081 item 2)
body:
Part of #12081 (item 2)
Clause-②: yes

A calendar view inside a list now draws every record of the days it shows. Before, it drew only the first 100 records of the object. Items 3, 4 and 7 of the card stay open, and #12081 is not addressed beyond item 2 here.

## What was measured on `main` (`5330afd`)

- **Where the 100 comes from (PM assumption 1: holds).** `ListView` makes one unpaged fetch for every view except the flat grid. Its `$top` is `effectivePageSize`, which falls back to `DEFAULT_LIST_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE` (100), and it carries no date condition. The rows are handed to the `object-calendar` node as `data`. The renderer forwards an array `data`, and `ObjectCalendar` then skips its own fetch. That fetch is the one that carries the ruling a′ ceiling (2,001 with the probe row) and its footnote. So the hotclm reading `top=100&select=…,end_date` is this fetch, and its only sign was the list's "Showing first 100 records" note.
- **Reproduced red on `main`.** New pin `ListView.calendarDateWindow-12081`, case (a), with only the test file present: `AssertionError: expected [ 'sep-0', 'sep-1', 'sep-2', …(97) ] to include 'oct-60'`. The calendar was handed the first 100 rows of the object, mostly from the month before.
- **Where the visible range lives (PM assumption 3).** It is `ObjectCalendar` state (`currentDate`, `view`), which `CalendarView` mirrors. The month grid is 42 days from the display locale's first day of the week, and on a phone the view switches to day by itself. `ListView` received none of it: it passed neither `onNavigate` nor `onViewChange`, and neither one fires for the state the calendar opens on.
- **The three texts are compatible (PM assumption 2).** Windowing and paging need no authorable key. The range reaches the fetch through one new host prop and nothing else.

## What changed

- **One fetch owner: `ListView`** (`calendarWindowed`). With a start binding, the calendar view's fetch selects the visible days on `startDateField`. With an `endDateField` bound, it selects every span that touches them. It also selects the records with no start date, so `ObjectCalendar`'s Unscheduled area keeps its records. The window node joins the effective filter under one `and`, so the view filter, panel, user filters and search still narrow it. The bounds are local `YYYY-MM-DD` dates, widened by one day on each side, so a UTC-stored instant always lands inside the window.
- **Walked in fetch-batch steps** (`fetchCalendarWindow` in the new `plugin-list/src/calendarWindow.ts`). Every request has `$top` at most 100, with `$skip` advancing. The walk stops at the first short batch, or one probe row past `NON_GRID_ROW_CEILING`. `applyNonGridRowCeiling` then cuts the result, and `ListView` draws `NonGridRowCeilingNote` under the calendar naming N and M. ⛔ No bigger cap. `dataLimitReached` stays off for a windowed calendar. The rows-per-page picker is withheld there, because a page size changes nothing the calendar draws.
- **The calendar reports its days:** `ObjectCalendarComponentProps.onVisibleRangeChange({ start, end })`. It fires on mount and whenever navigation or a view change moves the range. The range is half-open over local midnights. It is computed by `getVisibleDateRange`, built on the same `getMonthDays` and `getWeekStart` the grids draw with. Those two helpers moved verbatim from `CalendarView.tsx` into the new `plugin-calendar/src/visibleDays.ts`, so the report also survives the tests that stub the `CalendarView` module. The effect is keyed on the two instants, and the callback is read through a ref, so an unchanged range is never reported twice. The `object-calendar` renderer forwards it through its declared host-callback list, as it does `onNavigate`.
- **Navigation.** Until the first report, the window covers any month grid today can open on (`initialCalendarWindow`). So the first fetch does not wait for the calendar, and a host-registered calendar that never reports still draws today's month. The calendar's first report falls inside that window, so it asks for nothing more. A range the held window covers (a week of the same month, or the phone's day view) asks for nothing; one it does not cover fetches that window. A windowed calendar is not swapped for the list's loading skeleton, so it keeps the month it moved to across the refetch. It keeps drawing while the next window loads, under the existing refresh bar. Leaving the calendar view drops its window. This is done during render, so a calendar shown again opens on today's window.
- **Route note.** The other suggested route was "a hosted calendar fetches its own window". It would have taken the list's toolbar search off the calendar, because `ObjectCalendar`'s query has no search channel. It would also have broken the toolbar Refresh, the client-side export and the user-filter counts, all of which read this view's rows, and each would have needed another prop. So the fetch stays with `ListView`. The standalone `ObjectCalendar` fetch (no host `data`) is unchanged.
- **File surface.** The claimed surface was `ListView.tsx` and `ObjectCalendar.tsx` with their tests, plus the changeset. Named extensions: two new pure modules beside them (`calendarWindow.ts`, `visibleDays.ts`), the renderer's host-callback list in `plugin-calendar/src/index.tsx`, the `calendar` row of `ListView.pageSizeAndFetchBatch-9853` (it now asserts the walk: every step is the batch, never the page size), the cross-package pin in `app-shell` (the only package depending on both), and the docs that AGENTS.md's docs-driven rule asks for (`plugin-list` README's paging paragraph, which this change made false; `plugin-calendar` README; `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx`). `ListView`'s calendar branch keeps its own reads of the two bindings, which the `calendarUnionReads-8651` source pin reads. The window reads the same two expressions at component scope, with a comment tying the pair together.

## Clause-② (yes): what the published surface gains

- **Props:** one. `ObjectCalendarComponentProps.onVisibleRangeChange?: (range: { start: Date; end: Date }) => void`, optional.
- **Exports:** none. The `plugin-list` package entry is not in the diff. In `plugin-calendar`'s entry, only the `HOST_CALLBACKS` array changes. The new modules are not re-exported, and no `export *` exists in either entry.
- **Locale keys:** none. The footnote reuses `common.rowCeilingNote` / `common.rowCeilingNoteUnknownTotal`.
- **Authorable keys:** none. Nothing on `@object-ui/types` changes, and the view schema is unchanged.

## Tests (head `25e515d`)

- `ListView.calendarDateWindow-12081` (11 cases). (a): 122 October records with 40 August records listed ahead are all handed over; every step has `$top` at most 100; the walk takes more than one step; the filter names the field the calendar draws by; no out-of-grid month is handed over; no `data-limit-warning` appears. (b) twice: an uncovered range refetches December whole, and a covered range sends zero requests. (c): 2,050 records hand 2,000 rows, the walk asks for 2,001 in total, and the `role=note` footnote names 2000 and 2050. Also: a fitting window draws no note; undated records ride along; a span opening before the window is fetched; the view filter still narrows. CONTROLS: the paged grid's requests are a literal equal to before (`$top` = the spec display default, then `$skip` on page 2, no window); the board is still one batch with no filter; a calendar with no start binding keeps its single batch and gets no callback.
- `ObjectCalendar.visibleRange-12081` (6 cases): the month grid under `en-US` and `en-GB`, Next period, the week view, the day view, and no re-report on a fresh handler.
- `app-shell` `listCalendarDateWindow-12081`: the REAL `ListView` over the REAL `ObjectCalendar`. All 122 October chips are drawn. Next period draws all 110 November chips, and the header still reads November 2026.
- **Reverse check from committed `25e515d`.** The four product files were restored to `5330afd`, with each blob verified on disk. The predicted direction was red. Observed: `Tests 15 failed | 14 passed (29)` across the four pin files. The 14 passing are the CONTROL rows, the 9853 rows of the other views, the filter case, and the no-re-report case, which passes vacuously on `main`. The restore was `git checkout HEAD -- …`, with every blob equal to HEAD and `git diff HEAD` 0 bytes.
- **Package suites.** `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/ packages/plugin-calendar/ …listCalendarDateWindow-12081.test.tsx` gave `Test Files 188 passed (188)`, `Tests 1837 passed | 95 skipped`. That run was at `da0bab9`. `25e515d` changes only the window-state plumbing in `ListView.tsx` and the ref write in `ObjectCalendar.tsx`. After it, the 6 directly affected files are green (`56 passed`). The union re-run at `25e515d` is in progress, and its verdict lands in the `os-dev-report` comment on #12081.

## Gates (head `25e515d`)

- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-list type-check` and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-calendar type-check`: both scripts echoed `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, exit 0.
- Exit 0 each: `check:new-line-citations` (VERDICT 0 new citations), `check:control-bytes`, `check-changeset-presence` (10 source files of 3 released packages, 1 changeset), `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:test-path-roots`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`, `check:vi-mock-override-shape`, `check:esm-specifiers` (specifiers only), `check:self-import`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:spec-symbols`, `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-example-ids`. A raw control-byte self-scan of the changed files found 0.
- **Locale gates not owed:** no locale string changed.
- **NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports`.** Reason: it needs every package built (population floor 25), and this tree built only the closure. The README edits add no fenced block or import.
- **NOT MEASURED yet: `check:eager-closure`.** It needs a base and a head console build. The reading lands in the report.
- **Lint, narrowed, three parts.** ① The population is `eslint.config.js`'s `**/*.{ts,tsx}` blocks; the 10 touched `.ts`/`.tsx` files all fall in them. ② `--format json` read 10 files, 0 errors. ③ Invariance: the config has no `projectService`, `parserOptions.project` or `TypeChecked` preset, so linting is not type-aware and this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict. On added lines, the only non-`any` warnings sit on the two pre-existing dependency-array lines. Both exist on `main`: the fetch effect's are suppressed by its inline directive under `eslint .`, and the view memo's (`onColumnStateChange`) is a standing warning. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is declared to CI.

## Acceptance notes (observed, not filed)

- The standalone `ObjectCalendar` (no host `data`) still fetches its whole filtered set up to the a′ ceiling, with its footnote, rather than its visible window. It is loud, not silent, so it is not a defect. It could reuse `getVisibleDateRange`. Carrier: none.
- Walking by `$skip` relies on the backend answering the view's `$orderby`, or no order, stably between requests. The paged grid's pager relies on the same property. Carrier: none.
- Resolved in this PR by `b5a5d1b`: `content/docs/plugins/plugin-calendar.mdx` used to list "Date Filtering: Automatically filters records by date range" as an `ObjectCalendar` feature. The bullet now names the visible-day report, links the Visible days section, and says that the standalone component fetches its whole filtered set up to the row ceiling.
- The Tests and Gates sections above were read on `25e515d`. The landing head `b5a5d1b` adds only a `main` merge and prose: the `DEFAULT_LIST_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE` docblock, the 9853 pin's header, two changeset bullets and the mdx bullet. No code or assertion changed. Contract review `6105341715` is on `b5a5d1b`.
